input: Write weekly affirmations in a dedicated journal

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many affirmations to write per session and whether they are free-form or themed shapes the structure of each entry.
The specific day and time chosen for writing determines how the habit is scheduled and anchored into the user's routine.
Understanding who the affirmations are for — the user themselves, a relationship, a professional goal — changes the subject matter and tone entirely.
The style of affirmations (e.g., present-tense statements, gratitude-based, identity-based) significantly changes what the user actually writes.
Whether the user already has a journal or needs to choose one (physical vs. digital) is the most immediate next action before the habit can start.
A time limit per session tells us how deep or brief each entry should be, preventing the habit from feeling overwhelming.
Knowing what the user hopes to feel or achieve through this practice defines what 'done well' looks like and how to measure progress.

gold.taskTitle: Write weekly affirmations in a dedicated journal
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a regular habit of writing affirmations in a journal each week.

questions.title: How many affirmations will you write each week?
questions.description: Determine the target number of affirmations per weekly session — e.g., 3, 5, 10 — to define the scope of each entry.

questions.title: Which day and time will you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Pin down the specific day of the week and time of day to anchor the habit into the user's existing routine.

questions.title: What area of your life are the affirmations focused on?
questions.description: Identify whether the affirmations target self-confidence, health, relationships, career, or another life domain to keep entries purposeful.

questions.title: What style of affirmation resonates most with you?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user prefers present-tense 'I am' statements, gratitude-based phrases, identity affirmations, or another format.

questions.title: Will you use a physical notebook or a digital tool?
questions.description: Establish the medium for journaling — handwritten notebook, notes app, dedicated journaling app — as this is the first practical step.

questions.title: How much time will you spend writing each session?
questions.description: Set a realistic time cap per session so the habit feels sustainable and not burdensome.

questions.title: What do you hope to feel or achieve after a month of this?
questions.description: Define the intended outcome — e.g., more self-confidence, reduced anxiety, clearer goals — to measure whether the practice is working.
